title: introduce-kms-guardian-operator-and-helm-rotate-sealed-backups-with-terraform-module-bump
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds KMS Guardian operator for HSM-backed key lifecycle, Helm upgrade hooks to snapshot and rotate sealed-secrets backups (envelope encrypted with KEK), and bumps terraform/modules/kms to v2.4.0. Includes e2e upgrade/rollback tests and SoftHSM CI job.
description: Motivation: On private deployments customers require automated, auditable rotation of key encryption keys (KEKs) used to envelope-encrypt SealedSecrets and other installer-managed secrets while preserving the ability to roll back upgrades safely. This PR introduces a small on-cluster controller (kms-guardian) plus Helm upgrade hooks and a Terraform module bump to automate HSM-backed KEK rotation and safe sealed-secrets snapshotting. Summary of changes: 1) New component: kms-guardian operator (controller + CRD). Responsible for scheduling KEK rotations, orchestrating HSM key wrap/unwrap (PKCS#11 compatible), and writing rotation events to the installer's audit log. Operator supports dry-run and a "fastpath" test mode for SoftHSM in CI. 2) Helm chart changes: a post-upgrade hook creates an atomic snapshot of sealed-secrets (namespaced) into an S3-compatible bucket using an envelope encryption KEK pulled from the HSM. A pre-rollback hook validates that the snapshot decrypts with the previous KEK and aborts rollback if validation fails. Hooks are idempotent and expose TTL labels for retention. 3) Terraform module bump: terraform/modules/kms provider bumped to v2.4.0 with new resources for HSM policy statements and a new output to supply KEK metadata to the installer. 4) Installer bootstrap updates: bootstrap flow now includes an HSM policy verification step and optional SoftHSM fallback for dev/on-prem installs. 5) CI and tests: added e2e/upgrade-rollback tests that exercise rotation during a simulated upgrade and confirm rollback safety. Added a SoftHSM matrix to the e2e pipeline for validation. Checklist: - [x] Implement kms-guardian controller and CRD - [x] Add Helm post-upgrade and pre-rollback hooks - [x] Terraform module bump and documentation - [x] e2e upgrade/rollback tests and CI matrix - [x] Add audit log events and metrics (prometheus counters per rotation) - [x] Docs: README for operator and runbook for rotation/incident response How it works (high level): kms-guardian calls into the HSM via the PKCS#11 shim to create a new KEK version, then re-encrypts a per-namespace envelope key used to encrypt SealedSecrets payloads. The Helm post-upgrade hook runs an idempotent snapshot job that collects SealedSecrets CRs, encrypts the snapshot with the current KEK (HSM-wrapped), and uploads to customer-configured object storage. On rotate, kms-guardian coordinates a multi-step handoff: generate new KEK -> use HSM to wrap new KEK with HSM master -> update metadata and push new encrypted envelope keys -> signal readiness -> Helm hooks run validation where necessary. Rollback safety: pre-rollback hook decrypts a tiny marker payload from the snapshot using the previous KEK; if decryption fails the rollback is blocked and operators are alerted. Security considerations: operator never exports raw KEK material; all wrapping/unwrapping happens inside HSM or SoftHSM. Audit events include rotation initiator, rotation version, and thumbprints. Backwards compatibility: optional feature flag `installer.kmsGuardian.enabled`; default is off for older installs. Testing: added unit tests for the operator's state machine and integration tests that run against SoftHSM in the CI matrix. Also added a local-mode script for customers to validate HSM connectivity in air-gapped installs. Related: references ENG-9213 for product requirement and SEC-377 for threat-model signoff. Notes: this is intentionally conservative in scope — operator handles KEK lifecycle and orchestrates snapshot/validation but does not migrate application-level keys (outside installer-managed sealed-secrets). Future work: automate HSM failover integration and a CLI for manual rotation.
